findings.mechanism: setInterval timer created per session in startHeartbeat (called from src/gateway.js:23) is stored only on session.heartbeat and is never cleared. Session.close() (src/session.js:62-68) and Gateway.release() never call clearInterval. The active timer list holds the beat closure -> session -> socket (LoopbackSocket.written array of all frames sent to it), decoder, recent[64] messages. timer.unref() only stops it keeping the loop alive, it does not let it be collected. The beat() early-return on session.closed only runs after the heartbeat period (30s default) and the interval is never cancelled even then, so every closed session is retained for the process lifetime.
findings.evidence: Ran runWorkload(3000) in 4 waves with forced GC after each: heapUsed 16.0, 28.4, 40.6, 52.8 MB (about +12 MB per wave) with 0 open sessions. Control with the interval cleared in Session.close: 3.8, 4.0, 4.1, 4.1 MB, flat.
findings.discriminator: Growth disappears when clearInterval is added on close; sessions=0 yet heap grows.

findings.mechanism: Session.recent is capped at RECENT_LIMIT=64 via shift()
findings.evidence: Code inspection; the per-wave growth vanished in the control run where only the timer was cleared, so recent only matters because the timer pins the session.
findings.discriminator: Bounded at 64 entries and freed with the session once the timer is cleared.

findings.evidence: Session.close unsubscribes every topic and unsubscribe deletes empty topic entries; snapshot topics count returns to 0 after the load run.
findings.discriminator: topics Map empties once all sessions close.

findings.cause: key set is small and fixed
findings.evidence: Keys are fixed names plus closed_<reason> with a fixed set of reasons (socket, idle, bye, protocol); the latency array has a fixed length.
